maria: FYI rolled a tiny FP8 canary to a slice of the L40S pool (short-seq traffic only). Overall QPS looks fine but seeing 95/99p latency spikes for some batch shapes. stack: transformer_engine v0.12 + runtime v2.8.

ashwin: OK can you paste the percentile dump? also which kernel path selected (nvfuser vs te-gemm)?

maria: Pasted below (short run, same prompt):
```
batch_shape=8x512: p50=12ms p90=18ms p95=28ms p99=85ms
batch_shape=4x2048: p50=9ms  p90=14ms p95=20ms p99=70ms
throughput tokens/s ~ unchanged vs INT8 baseline
stack hint: selected kernel=te_fp8_gemm_fast (fallbacks to int8_slowpath seen)
```

perf-bot: profile uploaded -> https://perf.internal/3312345678/profile-abc123 (nvprof and TE trace).

ashwin: Looks like jitter is in the tail when KV cache hits are ~60-70%. Could be warmup eviction thrash + kernel handoff. Two quick ideas: (1) force the fallback policy to prefer FP8 slowpath consistently to avoid mid-request handoffs, (2) try precompiling the te kernels for the common shapes.

sophia: Agreed re: handoffs. Also our selector uses a latency-estimate heuristic that switches kernels when occupancy > threshold. If occupancy fluctuates during a request (micro-batching + KV replay), it can re-evaluate and swap kernels mid-req. We should avoid re-selection after enqueue.

tim: Repro steps I used locally:
```bash
# run a short canary repro on L40S image
TE_PRECOMPILE=true TE_KERNEL_SELECT_ON_ENQUEUE=false ./bin/run_infer --model gpt-7b --batch-shapes "8x512,4x2048" --kv-pattern warmstart
```
That `TE_KERNEL_SELECT_ON_ENQUEUE=false` prevents mid-request kernel re-eval and helped cut p99 by ~30% locally.

maria: oof that's promising. Any config knobs to try on the transformer engine side (we're on TE v0.12)?

ashwin: A couple: `transformer_engine.fp8_dynamic_calibration=true` (auto-adjusts FP8 scale but can add overhead), `transformer_engine.fp8_stability_mode=1` (safer math paths, slightly slower), and `te.gemm_kernel_preference=consistent`(our shim). Try toggling stability_mode first.

sophia: Also examine KV cache eviction window. If hotcache spinups cause many cold paths, you'll trigger different kernel footprints. Try increasing `kv.cache_warmup_ms` from 50->150 and `kv.eviction_batch_threshold` +20%.

maria: Running a 30m canary with these 3 changes: lock kernel-on-enqueue, fp8_stability_mode=1, kv_warmup_ms=150. Will post results in ~35m.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for fp8-l40s-canary (slice=5%) :rocket:

maria: quick interim result after 10m: p99 dropped from 85ms -> 28ms, p95 down to 22ms. throughput -3% on tokens/s. No sign of handoff logs in traces.

ashwin: Good. That suggests mid-request kernel handoff was the main culprit. Can you grep traces for `kernel_switch` events?

maria: grep shows 0 kernel_switch events after the change, previously we had ~2.4% requests with 1+ switch.

tim: Nice. Can we adopt `TE_KERNEL_SELECT_ON_ENQUEUE=false` as default for short/medium sequences? Maybe keep the dynamic selector for long-context where occupancy evolves gradually.

sophia: I'd rather we make it a selector policy: `sticky_after_enqueue=true` for batch_length < 4096. Less surprising than blanket global. Also add a metric for kernel_switch rate to console.

maria: Agreed on policy. Also note: enabling `fp8_stability_mode` fixed stability but cost ~3% throughput. Tradeoff looks acceptable for hosted defaults.

ashwin: Next experiments: (A) try `fp8_dynamic_calibration=false` + precompilation to see if we can regain that 3% without re-introducing jitter, (B) exercise mixed FP8/INT8 routing for very high occupancy shapes.

maria: I'll run (A) next. If results good, we'll flip sticky-on-enqueue policy for short seq canaries and add a rollout note.

perf-bot: baseline comparison artifact: https://perf.internal/3312345678/artifact-diff (contains nvtx timelines).

maria: Action items: 1) Prod config PR to add selector policy + metric (sophia/tim), 2) Run (A) fp8_dynamic_calibration=false + precompile (maria), 3) Dashboard tile for kernel_switch rate (prod-observability).

ashwin: :thumbsup:

maria: will update thread with final 30m numbers. Thanks all.
